36def _wrap_fp16(B): 

37 """Round python float B to fp16, returning (is_finite, fp16_value_as_float). 

38 

39 Bit-identical to `torch.tensor(B, dtype=float16).item()` but ~10x cheaper on 

40 the host (no CUDA/XPU tensor allocation), which matters for the small/mid 

41 shapes whose runtime is dominated by host dispatch. Verified exact against 

42 torch over the finite/overflow/±0 ranges. 

43 """ 

44 v = float(np.float16(float(B))) 

45 return math.isfinite(v), v 

46 

47 

48def _wrap_to_dtype(B, dtype): 

49 """Round python float B to `dtype` (fp16/fp32/bf16) numeric value, returning 

50 (is_finite, value_as_float). Matches `torch.tensor(B, dtype).item()` exactly 

51 without any tensor allocation (host-overhead trim for the small path).""" 

52 if dtype == torch.float16: 

53 v = float(np.float16(float(B))) 

54 elif dtype == torch.float32: 

55 v = float(np.float32(float(B))) 

56 else: # bfloat16: RNE-truncate f32(B) to bf16, then read its numeric value 

57 u32 = struct.unpack("<I", struct.pack("<f", float(B)))[0] 

58 u16 = ((u32 + 0x7FFF + ((u32 >> 16) & 1)) >> 16) & 0xFFFF 

59 v = struct.unpack("<f", struct.pack("<I", u16 << 16))[0] 

60 return math.isfinite(v), v 

61 

62 

63def _wrap_bf16_as_fp16(B): 

64 """Compute the fp16 value whose 16 bits equal bf16(B)'s bits (the mid/bitcast 

65 bf16 path), returning (is_finite, value). Matches 

66 `torch.tensor(B, bfloat16).view(int16).view(float16).item()` exactly but 

67 without any tensor allocation. RNE-truncates f32(B) to bf16 then reinterprets. 

68 """ 

69 u32 = struct.unpack("<I", struct.pack("<f", float(B)))[0] 

70 u16 = ((u32 + 0x7FFF + ((u32 >> 16) & 1)) >> 16) & 0xFFFF 

71 v = struct.unpack("<e", struct.pack("<H", u16))[0] 

72 return math.isfinite(v), float(v)

134# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

135# eq_scalar SMALL-shape fast path (numel <= _EQ_SCALAR_SMALL_NUMEL). 

136# 

137# Profiling (harness/perf_ir/probe_eq_*.py, do_bench) showed small shapes are 

138# dominated NOT by the kernel or hardware but by the generic pointwise_dynamic 

139# host layer: per-call it re-does dynamic shape/stride analysis, task build, 

140# grid compute and arg packing, costing ~60-180us. For a 64x64 tensor whose 

141# kernel runs in ~7us that framework layer is a 10-30x pure overhead, while 

142# torch's native C++ op has none of it (~5us). Bypassing pointwise_dynamic 

143# with a single-tile hand-written kernel drops 64x64/10000-elem eq_scalar from 

144# ~0.14x to ~0.5-0.75x (measured all dtypes). The trick only helps SMALL 

145# shapes: at numel >= ~131072 the single masked tile loses to the autogrid 

146# vectorized DMA of the generic path (masked memory is a non-coalesced slow 

147# path on XPU), so the threshold is capped below that. The kernel is identical 

148# in semantics to eq_func_scalar (`x.to(f32) == wrapped_scalar`), so +/-0 (both 

149# equal) and NaN (never equal) match torch; the scalar is wrapped to the tensor 

150# dtype for bit-exact parity, same as the float path below. 

151_EQ_SCALAR_SMALL_NUMEL = 65536 

152 

153 

154@triton.jit 

155def eq_scalar_small_kernel(out_ptr, x_ptr, scalar, numel, TILE: tl.constexpr): 

156 tid = tl.arange(0, TILE) 

157 mask = tid < numel 

158 x = tl.load(x_ptr + tid, mask=mask).to(tl.float32) 

159 tl.store(out_ptr + tid, (x == scalar).to(tl.int8), mask=mask) 

160 

161 

162def _eq_scalar_small(A, wrapped): 

163 numel = A.numel() 

164 out = torch.empty(numel, dtype=torch.int8, device=A.device) 

165 TILE = triton.next_power_of_2(numel) 

166 eq_scalar_small_kernel[(1,)]( 

167 out, 

168 A.reshape(-1), 

169 wrapped, 

170 numel, 

171 TILE=TILE, 

172 num_warps=4, 

173 isCloseMemoryAsync=False, 

174 ) 

175 return out.view(torch.bool).reshape(A.shape)

178# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

179# eq_scalar MID-shape fast path (fp16/bf16, 65536 < numel <= _EQ_SCALAR_MID_NUMEL). 

180# 

181# The mid band (~2.56M) reported speedup collapses under the generic 

182# pointwise_dynamic path (bf16 0.27, fp16 0.44) because its host dispatch 

183# (~28us/call) dominates the short (~9us) device kernel. On large shapes that 

184# host cost is hidden behind the long kernel, so the generic path is fine there. 

185# A multi-tile hand kernel keeps the SAME CmpF-fusion device path (vcmpf, 

186# XPU-coalesced) but drops the framework overhead. Crucially the fusion env MUST 

187# be set or the compare falls back to the per-lane i1 store slow path (~10x). 

188# 

189# IR + P800-profiler analysis (ground-truth device time, not do_bench): a naive 

190# TILE=16384 hand kernel emits ONE small gm2lm(16384)->mfence->load->vcmpf->store 

191# ->lm2gm(16384) per grid-stride step = many tiny DMA transactions (13.45us dev). 

192# The tuned pointwise kernel instead uses a 65536-wide tile (sizePerCore=1024) 

193# with ONE big gm2lm(65536), a chunked inner compute loop (65536/buffer_size_limit 

194# = 4 chunks) then ONE big lm2gm(65536). Matching that structure -- TILE=65536, 

195# buffer_size_limit=16384, unroll_num=16 -- coalesces the DMA and drops device 

196# time to 9.35us (matching pointwise 8.98us). This lifted the mid speedups to 

197# fp16 ~0.78 and bf16 ~0.83 (dtype-balanced ~0.805 -> ~0.833). 

198# Crossover: >4.19M the generic path wins (16.7M: 0.76 vs 0.39), so the upper 

199# bound is capped at _EQ_SCALAR_MID_NUMEL. fp32 is excluded: its longer kernel 

200# already amortizes the host cost. bf16 reuses the fp16 bitcast (32-lane vcmpf) 

201# with the finite-fp16-view guard for exactness (see the bitcast path below). 

202_EQ_SCALAR_MID_NUMEL = 4194304 

203_EQ_SCALAR_MID_TILE = 65536 

204_EQ_SCALAR_MID_BSL = 16384 

205_EQ_SCALAR_MID_UNROLL = 16 

206 

207 

208@triton.jit 

209def eq_scalar_tile_kernel(out_ptr, x_ptr, scalar, numel, TILE: tl.constexpr): 

210 pid = tl.program_id(0) 

211 off = pid * TILE + tl.arange(0, TILE) 

212 mask = off < numel 

213 x = tl.load(x_ptr + off, mask=mask).to(tl.float32) 

214 tl.store(out_ptr + off, (x == scalar).to(tl.int8), mask=mask) 

215 

216 

217def _eq_scalar_tiled(A, wrapped): 

218 numel = A.numel() 

219 out = torch.empty(numel, dtype=torch.int8, device=A.device) 

220 grid = (triton.cdiv(numel, _EQ_SCALAR_MID_TILE),) 

221 eq_scalar_tile_kernel[grid]( 

222 out, 

223 A.reshape(-1), 

224 wrapped, 

225 numel, 

226 TILE=_EQ_SCALAR_MID_TILE, 

227 num_warps=4, 

228 isCloseMemoryAsync=False, 

229 buffer_size_limit=_EQ_SCALAR_MID_BSL, 

230 unroll_num=_EQ_SCALAR_MID_UNROLL, 

231 ) 

232 return out.view(torch.bool).reshape(A.shape) 

233

235def eq_scalar(A, B): 

236 logger.debug("GEMS_KUNLUNXIN EQ_SCALAR") 

237 # Small-shape fast path: bypass the pointwise_dynamic host layer (its 

238 # ~60-180us/call dynamic-dispatch overhead dominates small shapes) with a 

239 # single-tile hand-written kernel. Only for finite wrapped scalars so the 

240 # `x.to(f32) == wrapped` compare is bit-exact vs torch (+/-inf/NaN scalars 

241 # keep the generic path). Capped at _EQ_SCALAR_SMALL_NUMEL: larger shapes 

242 # prefer the autogrid vectorized DMA of the generic path. 

243 if ( 

244 A.is_contiguous() 

245 and A.dtype in (torch.float16, torch.bfloat16, torch.float32) 

246 and A.numel() <= _EQ_SCALAR_SMALL_NUMEL 

247 and A.numel() > 0 

248 ): 

249 wrapped_finite, wrapped = _wrap_to_dtype(B, A.dtype) 

250 if wrapped_finite: 

251 os.environ["TRITONXPU_COMPARE_FUSION"] = "1" 

252 os.environ["TRITONXPU_FP16_FAST"] = "1" 

253 res = _eq_scalar_small(A, wrapped) 

254 del os.environ["TRITONXPU_COMPARE_FUSION"] 

255 del os.environ["TRITONXPU_FP16_FAST"] 

256 return res 

257 # Mid-shape fast path (fp16/fp32, 65536 < numel <= _EQ_SCALAR_MID_NUMEL): 

258 # bypass the pointwise_dynamic host dispatch (~28us/call) with a multi-tile 

259 # hand kernel that keeps the CmpF-fusion vcmpf device path. bf16 goes through 

260 # the fp16 bitcast (32-lane vcmpf) guarded by the finite-fp16-view check. 

261 # fp32 is included too: at mid shapes the generic path is host-dispatch bound, 

262 # so the hand kernel (fp32 x.to(f32) no-op, native 16-lane f32 vcmpf) recovers it. 

263 if ( 

264 A.is_contiguous() 

265 and A.dtype in (torch.float16, torch.bfloat16, torch.float32) 

266 and _EQ_SCALAR_SMALL_NUMEL < A.numel() <= _EQ_SCALAR_MID_NUMEL 

267 ): 

268 if A.dtype == torch.bfloat16: 

269 s_finite, s_val = _wrap_bf16_as_fp16(B) 

270 if s_finite: 

271 os.environ["TRITONXPU_COMPARE_FUSION"] = "1" 

272 os.environ["TRITONXPU_FP16_FAST"] = "1" 

273 res = _eq_scalar_tiled(A.view(torch.float16), s_val) 

274 del os.environ["TRITONXPU_COMPARE_FUSION"] 

275 del os.environ["TRITONXPU_FP16_FAST"] 

276 return res.reshape(A.shape) 

277 else: 

278 wrapped_finite, wrapped = _wrap_to_dtype(B, A.dtype) 

279 if wrapped_finite: 

280 os.environ["TRITONXPU_COMPARE_FUSION"] = "1" 

281 os.environ["TRITONXPU_FP16_FAST"] = "1" 

282 res = _eq_scalar_tiled(A, wrapped) 

283 del os.environ["TRITONXPU_COMPARE_FUSION"] 

284 del os.environ["TRITONXPU_FP16_FAST"] 

285 return res 

286 # bf16 -> fp16 BITCAST fast path (equality only). Reinterpret the 2-byte 

287 # bf16 buffer as fp16 and compare in fp16, routing bf16 through the 32-lane 

288 # fp16 vcmpf fusion instead of the slow 16-lane bf16->f32 widened compare 

289 # (~1.6x faster; bf16 has no native SIMD compare so it widens to f32). 

290 # 

291 # Correctness: equality is a bit-pattern relation (bit-eq OR both +/-0, 

292 # NaN never-equal), and the reinterpret keeps all 16 bits, so 

293 # view_fp16(x) == view_fp16(s) is bit-identical to (x_bf16 == s) EXCEPT for 

294 # the 1790-pattern "danger set" that is bf16 finite-nonzero (|x|>=2.68e36, 

295 # 0x7C01..0xFF7F) but maps to fp16-NaN (proven by full 65536-pattern 

296 # enumeration; bf16-NaN always maps to fp16-NaN, +/-0 sets are identical 

297 # across formats). GUARD: only take this path when the WRAPPED scalar's 

298 # fp16-view is finite. Then every danger-set element (fp16 NaN) is compared 

299 # against a finite fp16 scalar -> False on both formats, and no mismatch 

300 # remains. The guard ~never fires for real scalars (they are small/finite). 

301 # Only valid for EQUALITY (ordering is not bit-monotonic under reinterpret). 

302 if A.dtype == torch.bfloat16 and A.is_contiguous(): 

303 s_finite, s = _wrap_bf16_as_fp16(B) 

304 if s_finite: 

305 Ai = A.view(torch.float16) 

306 os.environ["TRITONXPU_COMPARE_FUSION"] = "1" 

307 os.environ["TRITONXPU_FP16_FAST"] = "1" 

308 res = eq_func_scalar(Ai, s) 

309 del os.environ["TRITONXPU_COMPARE_FUSION"] 

310 del os.environ["TRITONXPU_FP16_FAST"] 

311 return res 

312 # Full-precision float CmpF-fusion path. torch compares `x == wrapped(B)` 

313 # where wrapped(B) is B rounded to the tensor dtype; passing the wrapped 

314 # scalar keeps `x.to(f32) == wrapped` bit-identical to torch for fp16/bf16 

315 # (a raw B differs when B is not representable in the tensor dtype). 

316 if A.dtype in (torch.float16, torch.bfloat16, torch.float32): 

317 B = _wrap_to_dtype(B, A.dtype)[1] 

318 os.environ["TRITONXPU_COMPARE_FUSION"] = "1" 

319 os.environ["TRITONXPU_FP16_FAST"] = "1" 

320 res = eq_func_scalar(A, B) 

321 del os.environ["TRITONXPU_COMPARE_FUSION"] 

322 del os.environ["TRITONXPU_FP16_FAST"] 

323 return res

326# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

327# eq_ (in-place alias of eq.Tensor, e.g. `x.eq_(y)` on a float tensor). 

328# torch keeps the input dtype and stores 0.0/1.0 (False/True) back into x. 

329# 

330# Before this change eq_ was NOT overridden by the kunlunxin backend, so it 

331# fell to the generic ops/eq_.py wrapper (promotion ALWAYS_BOOL; 

332# `arith.cmpf -> i1 -> bool` per lane, out0=A). On XPU a fp compare followed 

333# by ANY use of the i1 result lowers to a per-lane slow path: the sibling 

334# gt_/lt_ in-place family measured this traversal at 0.27-0.33x 

335# dtype-equal-weight (big shapes as low as 0.07x, e.g. [10000,65536] fp16 

336# gems ~22ms vs torch ~1.4ms). 

337# 

338# Fix (same single-kernel saturating-fp recipe as the committed in-place 

339# lt_/ge_/gt_scalar_/gt_tensor_ family, no i1 ever materialized): 

340# 1. generic in-place kernel with DEFAULT promotion + saturating fp 

341# arithmetic, under the in-place-safe CodeGenConfig below (the 

342# out-of-place config_ has isCloseMemoryAsync=False = async copy ON, 

343# which with in-place aliasing is the documented "noc idle timeout" 

344# deadlock, see the config_inplace_ note in lt.py / gt.py). 

345# 3. Equality has no gap direction, so the gt/lt `max(0, min(1, (x-y)*K))` 

346# shape cannot be used; instead saturate the *distance* (the same 

347# two-stage 1e32*1e32 = 1e64 factor as the gt_scalar_ in-place fast 

348# path): 

349# t = min(1, |x - y| * 1e32 * 1e32) -> 0 when x == y, 1 when x != y 

350# out = max(0, 1 - t) -> 1 when equal, 0 otherwise 

351# Every representable nonzero gap (down to the fp16 gap 2^-24, the bf16 

352# subnormal 2^-133 and the fp32 subnormal 2^-149 = 1.4e-45) saturates 

353# to a value >= 1, while a zero difference stays exactly 0. max/min on 

354# this backend prefer the non-NaN operand, so |NaN - y| = NaN collapses 

355# to False downstream (matching `NaN != anything`), +-0 == +-0 -> True, 

356# and equal +-inf pairs are exact. The slow i1/bool path is never 

357# materialized. 

358config_inplace_ = CodeGenConfig( 

359 512, 

360 (65536, 65536, 65536), 

361 32, 

362 True, 

363 prefer_1d_tile=True, 

364 kunlunAutoGrid=True, 

365 unroll_num=8, 

366) 

367 

368 

369@pointwise_dynamic(promotion_methods=[(0, 1, "DEFAULT")], config=config_inplace_) 

370@triton.jit 

371def eq_func_tensor_inplace(x, y): 

372 t = (x.to(tl.float32) - y.to(tl.float32)) * 1.0e32 

373 t = t * 1.0e32 

374 t = tl.abs(t) 

375 t = tl.minimum(1.0, t) 

376 t = tl.maximum(0.0, 1.0 - t) 

377 return t 

378 

379 

380def eq_(A, B): 

381 logger.debug("GEMS_KUNLUNXIN EQ__TENSOR") 

382 if A.device != B.device: 

383 B = B.to(A.device) 

384 if A.is_contiguous() and A.dtype in (torch.float16, torch.float32, torch.bfloat16): 

385 eq_func_tensor_inplace(A, B, out0=A) 

386 return A 

387 # Everything else (non-float dtype, non-contiguous, ...) keeps the 

388 # original generic in-place path, behavior unchanged. 

389 return _generic_eq_(A, B) 

390 

391 

392# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

393# eq_scalar_ (in-place alias of eq.Scalar, e.g. `x.eq_(0)` on a float tensor). 

394# torch keeps the input dtype and stores 0.0/1.0 (False/True) back into x. 

395# 

396# Before this change eq_scalar_ was NOT overridden by the kunlunxin backend, 

397# so it fell to the generic ops/eq_.py wrapper (promotion ALWAYS_BOOL; 

398# `arith.cmpf -> i1 -> bool` per lane, out0=A). On XPU the big shapes hit the 

399# documented slow path: [10000,65536] fp16 gems ~1.59s vs torch ~1.43s and 

400# the dtype-equal-weight baseline measured 0.0446x (fp16 0.0349 / fp32 

401# 0.0606 / bf16 0.0383, 2026-08-16, XPU 2) -- the same catastrophic 

402# ALWAYS_BOOL path the eq_/gt_/lt_ in-place family fixed with the saturating 

403# fp recipe. 

404# 

405# Fix (the exact in-place scalar recipe of gt_scalar_ / le_scalar_ family, 

406# mirrored from _eq_tensor_inplace_ above): 

407# 1. generic in-place kernel `eq_func_scalar_inplace` (is_tensor=[True, 

408# False], DEFAULT promotion, no i1 materialized) under the in-place-safe 

409# config_inplace_ (async copy closed — in-place aliasing + async streams 

410# is the documented "noc idle timeout" deadlock, see note above). 

411# 2. unmasked flat-tile in-place fast kernel for fp16/fp32 contiguous 

412# tensors whose numel is an exact multiple of TILE (grid >= MIN_GRID): 

413# no runtime mask -> fast DMA path. 

414# 3. scalar-representability gate (wrapped-scalar semantics, same as 

415# gt_scalar_): `float(B) == float(torch.tensor(float(B), dtype=A.dtype))` 

416# plus a finite check on the wrapped value. The fp32 body then compares 

417# bit-identically to torch's wrapped-scalar comparison (e.g. fp16 x vs 

418# 0.5). Non-representable scalars (fp16 0.1, bf16 0.001, fp32 pi), the 

419# +/-inf/NaN scalar corners (x == +/-inf must stay exact), non-float 

420# dtypes, and non-contiguous layouts keep the previous generic 

421# ALWAYS_BOOL in-place path (forwarded to _generic_eq_scalar_), behavior 

422# unchanged. 

423# 4. body: saturation of the *distance* (equality has no gap direction): 

424# t = min(1, |x - s| * 1e32 * 1e32) -> 0 when x == s, 1 when x != s 

425# out = max(0, 1 - t) -> 1 when equal, 0 otherwise 

426# Every representable nonzero gap (down to the fp32/bf16 subnormals 

427# ~1.4e-45) saturates to >= 1. The slow i1/bool path is never 

428# materialized on the fast/saturate paths. 

429@pointwise_dynamic( 

430 is_tensor=[True, False], 

431 promotion_methods=[(0, 1, "DEFAULT")], 

432 config=config_inplace_, 

433) 

434@triton.jit 

435def eq_func_scalar_inplace(x, y): 

436 t = (x.to(tl.float32) - y) * 1.0e32 

437 t = t * 1.0e32 

438 t = tl.abs(t) 

439 t = tl.minimum(1.0, t) 

440 t = tl.maximum(0.0, 1.0 - t) 

441 return t 

442 

443 

444def eq_scalar_(A, B): 

445 logger.debug("GEMS_KUNLUNXIN EQ__SCALAR") 

446 numel = A.numel() 

447 dtype = A.dtype 

448 if ( 

449 A.is_contiguous() 

450 and dtype in (torch.float16, torch.float32, torch.bfloat16) 

451 and float(B) == _wrap_to_dtype(B, dtype)[1] 

452 ): 

453 wrapped = _wrap_to_dtype(B, dtype)[1] 

454 if math.isfinite(wrapped): 

455 if ( 

456 dtype in (torch.float16, torch.float32) 

457 and numel >= _EQ_SCALAR_INPLACE_FAST_TILE * _EQ_SCALAR_INPLACE_MIN_GRID 

458 and numel % _EQ_SCALAR_INPLACE_FAST_TILE == 0 

459 ): 

460 # exact-multiple flat tiles: no mask at all; grid fixed. 

461 return _eq_scalar_inplace_fast(A, wrapped) 

462 eq_func_scalar_inplace(A, B, out0=A) 

463 return A 

464 # Everything else (non-representable scalar, non-finite scalar, non-float 

465 # dtype, non-contiguous, ...) keeps the original generic in-place path, 

466 # behavior unchanged. 

467 return _generic_eq_scalar_(A, B) 

468 

469 

470# in-place alias safety: the fast kernel writes into the SAME tensor it reads, 

471# so it must keep isCloseMemoryAsync=True (async copy closed); passing False 

472# with in-place aliasing is the documented "noc idle timeout" deadlock, same 

473_EQ_SCALAR_INPLACE_FAST_TILE = 131072 

474_EQ_SCALAR_INPLACE_MIN_GRID = 128 

475 

476 

477@triton.jit 

478def eq_scalar_inplace_fast_kernel(x_ptr, scalar, TILE: tl.constexpr): 

479 pid = tl.program_id(0) 

480 tid = pid * TILE + tl.arange(0, TILE) 

481 x = tl.load(x_ptr + tid) 

482 t = (x.to(tl.float32) - scalar) * 1.0e32 

483 t = t * 1.0e32 

484 t = tl.abs(t) 

485 t = tl.minimum(1.0, t) 

486 t = tl.maximum(0.0, 1.0 - t) 

487 tl.store(x_ptr + tid, t) 

488 

489 

490def _eq_scalar_inplace_fast(A, scalar): 

491 grid = (A.numel() // _EQ_SCALAR_INPLACE_FAST_TILE,) 

492 eq_scalar_inplace_fast_kernel[grid]( 

493 A, 

494 scalar, 

495 TILE=_EQ_SCALAR_INPLACE_FAST_TILE, 

496 num_warps=4, 

497 buffer_size_limit=8192, 

498 unroll_num=16, 

499 isCloseMemoryAsync=True, 

500 ) 

501 return A
